question: Wen muss ich kontaktiern wenn ich problem mit barrierefreiheit oder accessibilty auf ost.ch hab und wie sind die editorial guidelines dafür gereglt?
reference_answer: Wenn Sie ein Problem mit Barrierefreiheit oder Accessibility auf ost.ch haben, sollten Sie das Marketing OST kontaktieren, da dieses Team für Barrierefreiheit / Accessibility sowie für die Optimierung der Website und Rechteverwaltung zuständig ist. Die Kontaktadresse lautet marketing@ost.ch (Roland Seeger, Patrick Aebersold, Stepan Kopec). Die redaktionellen Richtlinien (editorial guidelines) werden von der Kommunikation vorgegeben und gelten sowohl in Deutsch als auch in Englisch. Die Kommunikation unterstützt zudem initial bei redaktionellen Fragen. Für redaktionelle Fragen und die Koordination englischer Übersetzungen können Sie sich an die Kommunikation wenden: online-redaktion@ost.ch (Nicole Widmer, Muriel Grau).

question: How did the harmonization of processes around the Student Life Cycle for continuing education at OST, as described in the context of the fusion process and new legal frameworks, lead to specific revisions and adaptations in the Ausführungsbestimmungen (AFB) for various study programs, and what were some of the key changes discussed in the extraordinary university management meeting on February 14, 2022?
reference_answer: The harmonization of processes around the Student Life Cycle for continuing education at OST was implemented as part of the fusion process, which included the adjustment of framework conditions such as the study and examination regulations and their implementing provisions. This harmonization aimed to clarify structures of competencies and responsibilities in and around the processes of continuing education at OST. As a result, new requirements for the Ausführungsbestimmungen (AFB) became apparent, particularly regarding the proper handling of matters such as the allocation, withdrawal, or transfer of ECTS credits, as well as exmatriculation and changes in study forms. These requirements were identified by the study administration and were essential for the Student Life Cycle process. In response, the extraordinary university management meeting on February 14, 2022, discussed and enacted revisions to the AFB for several study programs, including Bachelor’s programs in Architecture, Landscape Architecture, Civil Engineering, Spatial Planning, Informatics, Renewable Energies and Environment, Industrial Engineering, Business Administration, Management and Law, and Business Informatics, as well as the Master’s program in Social Work. The meeting also addressed the need to align the names of study programs in the AFB titles with the diploma names according to the study and examination regulations, especially for the Department of Engineering. Additionally, the management delegated further revisions of the AFB for certain programs to relevant department heads and committees to ensure timely updates. These changes were based on experiences from the first semester under the new legal norms and aimed to correct errors and resolve inconsistencies with the curriculum, thereby supporting a more coherent and efficient Student Life Cycle process.
